title: Transport of cohomology along the geometric Frobenius
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] $p,a,q,k_0,k$, a
prime $\ell\neq p$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ contained in the chosen
algebraic closure $\Qlb$, an integer $n\geq1$, and a coefficient ring
$\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$, with the coefficient categories
$D^b_c(-,\Lambda)$ of [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility],
[def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed],
[def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] and
[def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Let $Y_0$ be a separated
finite-type [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] $k_0$-scheme, put
$Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$ and $s=\Spec k$, and let $a_Y:Y\to s$ be the structure
morphism, so that $Y$ is a separated finite-type $k$-scheme. Let
$\gamma=\operatorname{Frob}_q$, let
$g_Y=\operatorname{id}_{Y_0}\times\Spec(\gamma):Y\to Y$ be the geometric
Frobenius [def-weil-frobenius-detailed], and put $g_s=\Spec(\gamma):s\to s$;
by [lem-weil-frobenius-square-cartesian] (for $f_0=a_{Y_0}:Y_0\to\Spec k_0$)
$g_Y$ and $g_s$ are automorphisms, $a_Y\circ g_Y=g_s\circ a_Y$, and the
Frobenius square $(a_Y,g_Y,g_s)$ is Cartesian. Use the derived pullback
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], the derived direct image
[def-weil-derived-direct-image], the compact-support direct image
[def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], the point fiber functor
$\operatorname{Fib}_s$ [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], and the
cohomology complexes $\RGamma(Y,-)=\operatorname{Fib}_s(Ra_{Y*}(-))$ and
$\RGammac(Y,-)=\operatorname{Fib}_s(Ra_{Y!}(-))$ with their cohomology
groups $H^i(Y,-)$, $H^i_c(Y,-)$ [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology].
For $M\in D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$ the complex $Lg_Y^*M$ again lies in
$D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$ ([lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback] for
$\Lambda=A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E$, and stagewise for $\Lambda=E,\Qlb$), so
$\RGamma(Y,Lg_Y^*M)$ and $\RGammac(Y,Lg_Y^*M)$ are defined.

Let $\iota_N:\operatorname{Fib}_s(N)\to\operatorname{Fib}_s(Lg_s^*N)$, for
$N\in D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$, be the point transport
[def-weil-frobenius-point-transport], and let
$\operatorname{FrEx}_{Y,*}(M):Lg_s^*Ra_{Y*}M\to Ra_{Y*}Lg_Y^*M$ and
$\operatorname{FrEx}_{Y,!}(M):Lg_s^*Ra_{Y!}M\to Ra_{Y!}Lg_Y^*M$, for
$M\in D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$, be the direct-image and compact-support exchange
maps of the Frobenius square of $a_{Y_0}$
[def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange] (the case $f_0=a_{Y_0}$, $f=a_Y$ there).

The *transport of ordinary cohomology along $g_Y$* is the composite

$$
 \tau_M:\RGamma(Y,M)=\operatorname{Fib}_s(Ra_{Y*}M)
 \xrightarrow{\ \iota_{Ra_{Y*}M}\ }
 \operatorname{Fib}_s(Lg_s^*Ra_{Y*}M)
 \xrightarrow{\ \operatorname{Fib}_s(\operatorname{FrEx}_{Y,*}(M))\ }
 \operatorname{Fib}_s(Ra_{Y*}Lg_Y^*M)=\RGamma(Y,Lg_Y^*M),
$$

and the *transport of compactly supported cohomology along $g_Y$* is the
composite

$$
 \tau_{c,M}:\RGammac(Y,M)=\operatorname{Fib}_s(Ra_{Y!}M)
 \xrightarrow{\ \iota_{Ra_{Y!}M}\ }
 \operatorname{Fib}_s(Lg_s^*Ra_{Y!}M)
 \xrightarrow{\ \operatorname{Fib}_s(\operatorname{FrEx}_{Y,!}(M))\ }
 \operatorname{Fib}_s(Ra_{Y!}Lg_Y^*M)=\RGammac(Y,Lg_Y^*M).
$$

Both are natural in $M\in D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$, being composites of natural
transformations. For every integer $i$, $\mathrm H^i(\tau_M):H^i(Y,M)\to
H^i(Y,Lg_Y^*M)$ and $\mathrm H^i(\tau_{c,M}):H_c^i(Y,M)\to
H_c^i(Y,Lg_Y^*M)$ are the induced maps on cohomology groups. (These are the
maps by which $\operatorname{Gal}(k/k_0)$, and $W(k/k_0)$, act on
cohomology by transport of structure in Deligne, Weil II (1.1.7),
(1.1.11) and (1.1.14); that they are isomorphisms is
[lem-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport-iso].)

split_report.summary: Checked the definition against Deligne, Weil II (1.1.7), (1.1.10)-(1.1.11) and (1.1.14), pp. 150-152 (pdftotext), and against the slopmaster2 definitions def:weil-direct-image-object and def:weil-compact-support-object (FrEx_{f,*}, FrEx_{f,!}). Deligne only says that Gal/W act on fibres and on H^i, H^i_c 'par transport de structure'; the composite tau = Fib_s(FrEx) o iota is the blueprint's explicit form of this. Split by one level: the two auxiliary constructions the old statement defined inline became definition nodes, def-weil-frobenius-point-transport (iota_N, now without the inline claims that g_s^{-1}N(U)=N(g_s u) and Lg_s^*=g_s^{-1}: iota is defined by restriction, colimit insertion and the canonical map g_s^{-1}N -> Lg_s^*N, and its invertibility stays in lem-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport-iso) and def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange (FrEx_{f,*}, FrEx_{f,!} for any separated finite-type k_0-morphism f_0, as in slopmaster2, using the ambient exchange def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange, the open-square isomorphism b_g of lem-trf-open-square-exchange, the Cartesian open square lem-trf-frobenius-open-square and the existence of compactifications prop-compactification-refinement); the Cartesian property of the Frobenius square, asserted inline, became the statement node lem-weil-frobenius-square-cartesian. The constructibility of Lg_Y^*M, needed for RGamma(Y, Lg_Y^*M) to be defined and silent before, now points to lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback. stmt_deps: removed the six ids now used only inside the new exchange node (pbc-proetale-site, pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange, exchange-projection, compactifications-refinements, extension-by-zero, compactification-coherence), added the coefficient-category definitions, the three new nodes and lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback.

lean.note: All four coefficient cases use the recorded point-transport and canonical Frobenius-exchange maps, specialized to the actual geometric structure morphism. The compact recipe retains a model compactification over k₀. An exact ULift/scalar transport realizes the algebraically closed coefficient complex in D(Ω) with independent scheme and coefficient universes. The induced maps in every integer degree are explicit. No operation datum, arbitrary comparison, or new postponed theorem is assumed.
